reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is the Random Forest (RF), which constructs an ensemble of regression trees to estimate win probability (WP) from pre-play game states. Each tree partitions the feature space into bins based on splits chosen to maximize homogeneity of outcomes within bins. This process is repeated across bootstrapped samples and subsets of variables, ensuring diversity among trees. The final prediction is the average of individual tree predictions, yielding a smooth, nonparametric estimate of E[Y|X]. In GSI, this estimate serves as a prior for Bayesian inference, where posterior distributions are updated with new data. In GSE, it functions as a state transition kernel, mapping current game configurations to next-step probabilities. The method avoids strong parametric assumptions, making it robust to complex interactions between score differential, time remaining, field position, and down-distance. However, its reliance on historical data means it may fail under unprecedented game scenarios or when underlying dynamics shift significantly.
